issues.title: should attester present a PKCS10 object?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body: 6) Re: design goal 4, draft-novak-lamps-tacra-est has the attester presenting a PKCS #10 object, so it is not clear to me where this transparency line is being drawn (or if it is achievable). The transparency notion is muddied by the inclusion of the CAAPI client inside the attester and the fact that generating a CSR requires inputs that are not part of the proposed API, i.e., credential type would not have subject name.

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: The profile already puts names under the Credential Authority's policy ("MUST NOT mint identities (e.g., DNS names) beyond policy for the attested identity context"), and TACRA's Credential Hint section makes the hint a request, not an authorization. What may help is to say what the CSR is for here: proof of possession of CSKpri, not a statement of names. The Attester then needs no subject name: the reference CA takes the name from the Credential Hint or the CSR's common name and refuses anything outside policy ([est_server.py#L82-L84](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/est_server.py#L82-L84)). Suggest one sentence to that effect in the Enrollment section.

issues.title: where does key generation occur?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
10) Re: design goals in general, should there be a design goal focused explicitly on when/where key generation occurs, i.e., freshly generated by attester, freshly generated by CAS, factory generated, already held by the Secret Vault, etc.?  Should there be any goals related to attester identity (and attester authentication to the CAS in general)?
```

(I think this is EST related)

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: TACRA already places key generation in the Credential Acquisition Interface, inside the Attester (Architecture Meeting Design Goals: the CAI generates the CSK for Enrollment and the CEK for Retrieval); in the reference implementation both are fresh for each acquisition ([attester.py#L143](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/attester.py#L143), [attester.py#L164](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/attester.py#L164)). What the drafts do not say is that factory-provisioned keys and keys already held by a Secret Vault are out of scope; one sentence would settle Carl's list. On Attester authentication to the CAS: it is not needed for security, since the CAS is untrusted and the Attester's identity comes from its Evidence (TACRA, CAS Client Authentication to CAS Server). Leaving open for the out-of-scope sentence.

issues.title: secrets encrypted to CEKpub
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
11) Section 4.4 states "resulting secrets are encrypted to CEKpub, ensuring that only the Attester in possession of CEKpri can decrypt them". How does the secret vault establish that it should release a secret to CEKpub?
```

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: Two checks. The binding shows that CEKpub belongs to the attested environment: CEKpub is an input of the digest the Evidence carries, and the Secret Vault recomputes it with the CEKpub of the request before releasing anything ([est_server.py#L115](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/est_server.py#L115); rats-tacra PR #1, Binding Credential Keys to Evidence). The Vault's policy on the Attestation Results then decides which secret that environment may have ([est_server.py#L111](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/est_server.py#L111)). Ready to close once the binding PR is merged.

issues.title: How can EST/RFC7030 be used with AR?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```
12) Re: design goal 6, how can the API be used to support passport mode given it has no representation of Attestation Results? 
```

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: Already covered by the text. In the Passport model the CAS Server takes the Evidence to the Verifier and forwards the Attestation Results to the Credential Authority or Secret Vault (TACRA, Architecture Meeting Design Goals; this profile, step 7 of the Enrollment and Retrieval figures). The Attester never handles Attestation Results, which is how design goal 6 keeps the two models indistinguishable to it, so the API needs no representation of them. Closing; reopen if the text should say this more plainly.

issues.title: is Proof-of-Possession only way?
issues.author: mcr
issues.body:
```

15) In section 2, Credential Enrollment is defined only in terms of proof-of-possession credentials. That leaves no mode for a newly minted bearer token, e.g., a JWT issued on demand. Section 2 lists JWTs and API keys as Bearer Token Credentials and design goal 2 commits to supporting them. The API precludes them as Enroll-Credential requires a CSR and Retrieve-Credential is defined as fetching a pre-existing credential. Is it necessarily the case that only proof-of-possession credentials would require enrollment (especially given future proofing goals)?
```

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: TACRA already supports bearer tokens while discouraging them (Undesirability and Inevitability of Bearer Tokens), and delivers them sealed to CEKpub. A token minted on demand needs no new leg: the Relying Party mints it at release time and seals it to CEKpub with origin authentication, as a stored secret is released ([est_server.py#L115](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/est_server.py#L115)). So Enrollment can stay proof-of-possession with a CSR, and the definition of Retrieval can say "existing or newly minted".

comments.author: TheBankster
comments.body:
> TACRA already supports bearer tokens while discouraging them (Undesirability and Inevitability of Bearer Tokens), and delivers them sealed to CEKpub. A token minted on demand needs no new leg: the Relying Party mints it at release time and seals it to CEKpub with origin authentication, as a stored secret is released ([est_server.py#L115](https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/tacra-est/blob/dcca431/impl/est_server.py#L115)). So Enrollment can stay proof-of-possession with a CSR, and the definition of Retrieval can say "existing or newly minted".

Enrollment is for proof-of-possession credentials where the Attester holds the private key, which is unknown to any party outside of itself. Every other type of credential (pre-provisioned proof-of-possession credential or a bearer token credential) can be retrieved, not enrolled.
No change is necessary for this.

issues.title: Address incomplete EncryptedCredentialBundle TODO
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Per Grok's analysis, there is a critical blocker in submitting this draft. Listing the details below.

ISSUE: EncryptedCredentialBundle is still a TODO, IANA still registers it

```399:405:draft-novak-lamps-tacra-est.md
Mandatory-to-implement encryption mechanism: The specification MUST choose one baseline.
...
TODO: Ensure that TACRA architecture can carry these and other encryption mechanisms to the Attester in a predictable format.
```

`attest-retrieve` success and `application/est-attest-bundle+json` have no CDDL. The globalsign-est mock already has a concrete container (`enc`, `epk`, `nonce`, `ciphertext`, AAD over `group_id`/`target`/`handle`/`credential_hint`, no `server_id`). Either write that (or HPKE) into `{{bundle}}` or drop the media-type registration from `-00`.

The draft’s AAD list still includes `server_id`. The implementation dropped it.


SUGGESTD SOLUTION:

Do not copy the globalsign-est mock into the draft. It is ECDH + HKDF + AES-GCM with a homemade `info` string, and the code already calls that a stand-in for HPKE. Rubber-stamping it would freeze non-standard crypto as the EST profile.

Keep `application/est-attest-bundle+json`. Put **HPKE Base** (RFC 9180) in that JSON object, with one MTI suite. That is the same shape as the mock (P-256, HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM), with a real key schedule. CMS EnvelopedData is the LAMPS-native alternative; it would change the media type and fight the rest of `attest-*`. Use CMS only if the WG insists.

---

### Design

- **MTI:** HPKE Base, `DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256)`, `HKDF-SHA256`, `AES-256-GCM` (RFC 9180 identifiers 0x0010, 0x0001, 0x0002).
- **CEK:** P-256. Request `cek_pub` is the DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo (id-ecPublicKey, prime256v1). HPKE `pkR` is the uncompressed SEC1 point from that SPKI.
- **Seal:** `SetupBaseS(pkR, info)` then `Seal(aad, plaintext)`.
- **`info`:** the ASCII string `est-attest-bundle`.
- **`aad`:** length-prefixed concatenation (same style as TACRA `binding_input`), not JSON:

```
aad = len32(group_id) || utf8(group_id)
   || len32(target)    || utf8(target)
   || len32(handle)    || handle
   || len32(hint)      || utf8(hint)
```

`len32` is a 32-bit big-endian length. `handle` and `hint` are empty (length 0) when absent. Drop `server_id`. Put `target` in the AAD (the implementation already does).

- **Plaintext:** JSON `CredentialBundle` (group_id, items, optional metadata).
- **Wire:** JSON `EncryptedCredentialBundle`. Outer `group_id` / `target` / `handle` / `credential_hint` are copies of the AAD fields so a client can build `aad` without decrypting.
- **`acceptable_cek`:** initiate returns `"HPKE-Base-P256-SHA256-A256GCM"` as the MTI token.

Cite RFC 9180 as **normative**. Remove the CMS/HPKE/COSE menu and the TODO.

The mock will not interoperate until it calls HPKE. That is the right follow-up in globalsign-est, not a reason to specify the homemade KEM.

---

### Replace `{{bundle}}`

```md
### Response: EncryptedCredentialBundle {#bundle}

The EST Server returns the container produced by the Secret Vault.
The EST Client and EST Server MUST treat it as opaque.

The container is JSON, media type `application/est-attest-bundle+json` ({{cddl}}).
Implementations MUST support HPKE Base {{RFC9180}} with DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256, and AES-256-GCM (HPKE identifiers 0x0010, 0x0001, 0x0002).
That suite is the string `HPKE-Base-P256-SHA256-A256GCM` in `enc` and in `acceptable_cek`.

`cek_pub` in the request is the DER encoding of a SubjectPublicKeyInfo (Section 4.1 of {{RFC5280}}) for id-ecPublicKey on prime256v1 ({{RFC5480}}).
The Secret Vault uses the uncompressed SEC1 point from that SPKI as the HPKE public key.

The Secret Vault encrypts as follows:

1. `info` is the ASCII string `est-attest-bundle` with no terminating NUL.
2. `aad` is
   `len32(group_id) || utf8(group_id) || len32(target) || utf8(target) || len32(handle) || handle || len32(hint) || utf8(hint)`,
   where `len32(x)` is the length of `x` in octets as a 32-bit big-endian unsigned integer, `handle` is the freshness element of the request or empty, and `hint` is the UTF-8 encoding of `credential_hint` or empty.
3. `plaintext` is the UTF-8 JSON of a CredentialBundle ({{cddl}}).
4. `(encapsulated_key, ciphertext) = Seal(SetupBaseS(pkR, info), aad, plaintext)` as in {{RFC9180}}.

Fields of EncryptedCredentialBundle:

* `group_id` (string, REQUIRED): the credential group ({{group-id}})
* `enc` (string, REQUIRED): `HPKE-Base-P256-SHA256-A256GCM`
* `target` (string, REQUIRED): the Target of the request
* `handle` (bytes, OPTIONAL): the freshness element when the request carried one
* `credential_hint` (string, OPTIONAL): the hint when the request carried one
* `encapsulated_key` (bytes, REQUIRED): HPKE `enc`
* `ciphertext` (bytes, REQUIRED): HPKE `ct`

The Attester rebuilds `aad` from those fields, runs `SetupBaseR(encapsulated_key, skR, info)`, and opens `ciphertext`.
It MUST reject the container unless `enc` is the MTI suite, `target` equals the request Target, and `handle` equals the request handle when one was sent.

CredentialBundle plaintext:

* `group_id` (string, REQUIRED): MUST equal the outer `group_id`
* `credential_items` (array, REQUIRED, at least one): each item has `type` (string) and `data` (bytes)
    * `x509-cert`: DER-encoded X.509 certificate
    * `ca-certs-pem`: PEM CA certificates
    * `pkcs8-key`: DER-encoded PKCS#8 private key (high risk; see {{security}})
    * `wic`, `wit`, `jwt`, `api-key`, `psk`: the credential octets of that type
* `metadata` (object, OPTIONAL): implementation-defined string keys (validity, refresh, rotation epoch, key identifiers)

A Secret Vault MAY use another HPKE suite or another mechanism if the Attester selected it from `acceptable_cek`.
This document does not define those suites.
```

Leave the `group_id` formula as an example in `{{group-id}}`. Do not put `credential_hint` in the group key as a MUST.

---

### Add to `est-attest.cddl`

```cddl
encrypted-credential-bundle = {
  group_id: text,
  enc: "HPKE-Base-P256-SHA256-A256GCM",
  target: text,
  ? handle: text .b64u bytes,
  ? credential_hint: text,
  encapsulated_key: text .b64u bytes,
  ciphertext: text .b64u bytes,
}

credential-bundle = {
  group_id: text,
  credential_items: [+ credential-item],
  ? metadata: { * text => text },
}

credential-item = {
  type: text,
  data: text .b64u bytes,
}
```

In `{{cddl}}` prose, drop “The EncryptedCredentialBundle is not defined here.”

---

### Front matter and initiate

```yaml
normative:
  RFC9180: HPKE
  RFC5280:
  RFC5480:
```

Initiate `acceptable_cek` for retrieve: at least `HPKE-Base-P256-SHA256-A256GCM`.

IANA for `application/est-attest-bundle+json` can stay: the payload is now defined.

---

### What this does not do

It does not make the current mock decryptable as-is (HPKE labeled KDF ≠ `hkdf.Key(..., epk, aad)`). It does not pick CMS. It does not keep the three-way TODO.

If LAMPS wants CMS instead, switch the retrieve response to `application/pkcs7-mime` AuthEnvelopedData (RFC 5083) and withdraw `est-attest-bundle+json`. That is a different profile, not a small edit.

issues.title: TACRA `{#binding}` defines the digest but the draft never fills those profile slots.
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Grok has flagged the following critical blocking issue, and suggested a solution.

TACRA `{#binding}` defines the digest over three values and **delegates the Retrieval subject encoding to this profile**:

```
binding_input = len32(freshness) || freshness
             || len32(target)    || target
             || len32(subject)   || subject
```

This draft never fills those profile slots. Two implementations that both “follow TACRA” will not recompute the same digest.

What is missing:

1. **Enrollment prose is incomplete.** `{{relationship}}` and `{{key-binding}}` say Evidence is produced over a digest of the finished CSR. TACRA’s digest also covers the freshness element and the Target. A substituted Target or replayed freshness still verifies if a reader follows only this document.
2. **Retrieval `subject`.** TACRA: “CEKpub in the encoding the Credential Acquisition Mechanism carries it in.” Here that is only “the octets of `cek_pub`.” SPKI DER vs raw SEC1 point vs HPKE public key is unspecified. globalsign-est uses SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER for the digest.
3. **Freshness element on the wire.** Request `handle` is required for every kind except `absent-none`, but the field is still described as a Freshness Handle. For `absent-timestamp` TACRA uses an 8-octet big-endian Unix timestamp; for `absent-epoch` a locally held marker. Neither encoding is written here.
4. **`binding.method` / `hash`.** CDDL is unconstrained `text`. The implementation uses `method: "binding-input"` and SHA-512 for a 64-octet freshness input. Direct vs Nested vs Provider-scoped (TACRA platform forms) are not named.

The JSON `binding` object still has no `binding-input` member (open issue; out of scope here). The digest lives in Evidence; `binding` only names how it was produced.

---

## Proposed fix

Add one EST binding section and point enrollment, retrieval, and `{{relationship}}` at it. Specify the octets this profile uses. Do not add a `binding-input` JSON field.

### 1. New section, after Common Structures (or immediately before `{{key-binding}}`)

```md
## EST Binding of Credential Keys to Evidence {#est-binding}

This profile uses the digest of Section "Binding Credential Keys to Evidence" of {{TACRA}}.
The Attester writes that digest into the Evidence freshness input (the Direct form of that section).
The Verifier reports the value it read.
The Credential Authority or Secret Vault recomputes the digest from the second-leg request and refuses the request with 403 Forbidden unless the two are equal.

This profile specifies the three octet strings of that construction as follows.

`freshness` is the freshness element of the request:

* `present-nonce` / `present-epoch`: the Freshness Handle returned by `attest-initiate`, the octets of request `handle`
* `absent-epoch`: the epoch marker the Attester already holds, the octets of request `handle`
* `absent-timestamp`: an 8-octet big-endian unsigned count of seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, the octets of request `handle`
* `absent-none`: empty (length 0); request `handle` is absent

`target` is the UTF-8 encoding of the request `target` member, compared as an exact octet string.

`subject` is:

* Enrollment: the DER encoding of the PKCS#10 CSR, the octets of request `csr`
* Retrieval: the DER encoding of a SubjectPublicKeyInfo (Section 4.1 of {{RFC5280}}) for the CEK, the octets of request `cek_pub`. For the MTI HPKE suite ({{bundle}}), that SPKI is id-ecPublicKey on prime256v1 ({{RFC5480}}).

The JSON `binding` object does not carry these octets. It names the method and hash:

* `method` (string, REQUIRED): `binding-input` for the Direct form above
* `hash` (string, REQUIRED for `binding-input`): `sha512` when the Evidence freshness input is 64 octets (AMD SEV-SNP REPORT_DATA, Intel TDX REPORTDATA)

Implementations of this profile MUST produce and accept `method` `binding-input` with `hash` `sha512`.
A Credential Authority or Secret Vault that does not recognize `method` refuses the request with 400 Bad Request.

The digest is SHA-512 of `binding_input` as {{TACRA}} defines it.
A platform whose freshness input is not 64 octets is outside this profile's mandatory method.
```

Cite RFC 5280 (and RFC 5480 if `{{bundle}}` uses P-256 HPKE) as informative or normative, matching how you treat them for the bundle.

### 2. Point the existing MUSTs at that section

**`{{key-binding}}` item 2**, replace the two paragraphs with:

```md
2. Evidence-to-CSR and Evidence-to-Freshness: the Evidence MUST carry the digest of {{est-binding}}, with the DER-encoded CSR as `subject`. The Credential Authority recomputes that digest from the request and refuses the request with 403 Forbidden on a mismatch; a substituted CSR, Target, or freshness element fails that check.
```

**`{{evidence-to-cek}}`:**

```md
The Evidence MUST carry the digest of {{est-binding}}, with the SubjectPublicKeyInfo octets of `cek_pub` as `subject`.
The Secret Vault recomputes that digest from the request and denies release with 403 Forbidden on a mismatch.
```

**`{{relationship}}`**, replace “the Evidence is produced over a digest that includes the finished CSR” with:

```md
the Evidence freshness input carries the digest of {{est-binding}}, which includes the finished CSR, so that Evidence cannot travel inside the CSR
```

### 3. Rename request `handle` in prose (CDDL name can stay)

Enrollment and retrieval field lists, same sentence:

```md
* handle (bytes): freshness element of {{est-binding}} — REQUIRED when `freshness_kind` is not `absent-none`; MUST be absent otherwise. For `present-nonce` and `present-epoch` it MUST equal the Handle returned by `attest-initiate`. For `absent-timestamp` it is the 8-octet timestamp. For `absent-epoch` it is the locally held epoch marker.
```

Leave initiate-response `handle` as “Freshness Handle”; only the second-leg field is overloaded.

### 4. Tighten CDDL

```cddl
binding = {
  method: "binding-input",
  hash: "sha512",
}
```

If you want other methods later:

```cddl
binding = {
  method: "binding-input",
  hash: "sha512",
} / {
  method: text .ne "binding-input",
  ? hash: text,
}
```

`-00` can use the first form.

---

That is the whole interoperability hole: three octet strings, one method token, one hash name. Nested and provider-scoped platforms stay out of the MTI until a later revision adds method values.

issues.title: As written, a client can POST `credential_type: wimse-wit` with a CSR and is told to parse PKCS#7. That is not implementable.
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Grok has flagged the following critical blocking issue and suggested a solution:

`attest-enroll` success is **simpleenroll**: `application/pkcs7-mime; smime-type=certs-only` (RFC 7030 §4.2.3). That payload is a CMS certs-only bag of X.509 certificates.

The same document lets `credential_type` be `x509` **or** `wimse-wit` on **both** enroll and retrieve:

```337:337:draft-novak-lamps-tacra-est.md
* credential_type (string, OPTIONAL): e.g., x509, wimse-wit
```

A WIT is a JWT with key confirmation. It is not a PKCS#7 certs-only object. There is no enroll media type, ASN.1, or processing for it.

TACRA Enrollment mints a new proof-of-possession credential of the requested type (X.509, WIC, WIT). Retrieval returns an existing credential of any type, wrapped to CEKpub. This EST profile implements Enrollment as RFC 7030 simpleenroll and Retrieval as an encrypted bundle. The wire already splits types; the field examples do not.

globalsign-est matches the wire: enroll returns one X.509 cert; `jwt` / `psk` / `api-key` / `wit` go through retrieve.

As written, a client can POST `credential_type: wimse-wit` with a CSR and is told to parse PKCS#7. That is not implementable.

---

## Proposed fix

For this profile, **enroll mints an X.509 certificate**. Every other Credential Type in this document is **retrieve**. Do not add WIT/WIC enroll responses in `-00`.

That matches EST, the media-type table, the CSR/PoP text, and the running code. WIC can wait: it is certificate-shaped, but it is not simpleenroll until someone specifies the bag.

### 1. Abstract / intro (enrollment bullet)

Leave it as PKCS#10 CSR → issued certificate. No change required unless you currently imply “any TACRA credential.”

### 2. `credential_type` tokens this profile uses

Put this once (Common Structures, or a short subsection under IANA / modes) and delete the “e.g., x509, wimse-wit” examples from both request field lists:

```md
## Credential Type tokens {#credential-type}

When `credential_type` is present, this profile uses these values:

* `x509`: an X.509 certificate {{RFC5280}}. Enrollment mints one; Retrieval MAY return a previously issued chain.
* `wic`: a WIMSE Workload Identity Certificate {{WIMSE}}. Retrieval only in this version.
* `wit`: a WIMSE Workload Identity Token {{WIMSE}}. Retrieval only.
* `jwt`: a JWT {{RFC7519}} used as a bearer token. Retrieval only.
* `api-key`: an API key. Retrieval only.
* `psk`: a pre-shared symmetric key. Retrieval only.
* `pkcs8-key`: a PKCS#8 private key. Retrieval only (see {{security}}).

`attest-enroll` mints `x509`.
If `credential_type` is present on `attest-enroll` and is not `x509`, the EST Server refuses the request with 400 Bad Request.
If it is omitted, the Credential Authority mints `x509`.

`attest-retrieve` MAY carry any of the tokens above.
The Secret Vault selects the group from Attestation Results and the hint ({{group-id}}); `credential_type` MAY further restrict which `credential_items` are included.
If the Vault will not honor the type, it denies release with 403 Forbidden.

This document does not request a registry of these tokens.
```

Cite WIMSE and RFC 7519 as informative if those names stay.

### 3. Enrollment request / response

Replace the `credential_type` bullet and the success paragraph:

```md
* credential_type (string, OPTIONAL): MUST be `x509` if present ({{credential-type}})
```

```md
### Response (Success)

On success, the EST Server returns the certificate produced by the Credential Authority
as for simpleenroll (Section 4.2.3 of {{RFC7030}}):
`application/pkcs7-mime; smime-type=certs-only`.
That bag contains the newly minted X.509 certificate and, at the Authority's option, its chain.
```

### 4. Retrieval request

```md
* credential_type (string, OPTIONAL): one of the tokens in {{credential-type}}; MUST NOT be used to request enrollment of a new key
```

If you take the HPKE bundle from critical #1, `credential_items[].type` should use the same tokens (`x509-cert` vs `x509`: pick one set and use it on both the request and the item).

### 5. Initiate

`credential_type` query parameter: same tokens. For a Target whose policy is enroll-only, a retrieve-only type is 403 (same as unknown Target). For retrieve-only Targets, `x509` is allowed if the Vault holds a cert chain.

### 6. Error Handling

```md
* 400 Bad Request: a request that does not match its definition ({{cddl}}), an `attest-initiate` GET with no `target`, or `attest-enroll` with a `credential_type` other than `x509`
```

### 7. IANA

Drop this sentence from `{#iana}` (it is the same hole, one layer up):

> This document also requests a registry of acceptable_evidence identifiers and credential_type identifiers (if not reused from existing registries).

Tokens live in `{#credential-type}` until a WG document wants a registry.

---

Do **not** invent a WIT enroll media type for `-00`. If someone later needs attested WIT minting, that is a new enroll response (for example `application/at+jwt`) and a new `credential_type` rule, not a PKCS#7 bag.

issues.title: Clarify Passport and Background Check against RFC 9334 (CAS-relayed Verifier vs RP-contacted Verifier)
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Grok has flagged the following Important issue and suggested a solution:

Architecture says the EST encoding is the same in Passport and Background Check, then:

> The modes differ in 1) who originates a Freshness Handle and 2) whether the EST Server contacts the Verifier and then the RATS Relying Party (Passport) or the RATS Relying Party directly (Background Check).

Enrollment/retrieval processing repeats that split (steps 3–4). Figures are labeled Passport only.

That naming does not match RFC 9334:

- RFC 9334 Passport: the **Attester** sends Evidence to the Verifier, **holds** Attestation Results, and presents them to the Relying Party.
- RFC 9334 Background Check: the Attester sends Evidence to the Relying Party; the RP talks to the Verifier.

This profile (and TACRA, because the Attester has no network) uses:

- “Passport”: EST Server → Verifier → Credential Authority / Secret Vault. The Attester never sees AR.
- “Background Check”: EST Server → RP with Evidence; the RP talks to the Verifier.

From RFC 9334, both EST modes are Background-Check-shaped at the Attester. Handle origin (Verifier vs RP) is orthogonal to that split; TACRA already treats it separately.

LAMPS readers know RFC 9334. Leading with “Passport” as if it were RFC 9334 §5.2 will be misread.

**Suggested solution**

Keep TACRA’s two server topologies (they are real). Add one mapping paragraph in Architecture and stop using Handle origin as a distinguishing feature of the two modes. For example:

```md
The EST encoding is the same in both RATS topologies. The Attester does not talk to the Verifier and does not hold Attestation Results (Goal 8 of {{TACRA}}).

This profile uses the TACRA names:

* Passport: the EST Server forwards Evidence to the Verifier and forwards Attestation Results to the Credential Authority or Secret Vault.
* Background Check: the EST Server forwards Evidence to the Credential Authority or Secret Vault, which obtains Attestation Results itself.

In RFC 9334, Passport is the Attester holding Attestation Results. Both topologies here are Background Check from the Attester's point of view; they differ only in whether the EST Server or the RATS Relying Party contacts the Verifier.

Who originates a Freshness Handle (Verifier or RATS Relying Party) is independent of that split ({{TACRA}}).
Only the Passport topology is illustrated.
```

Leave processing steps 3–4 as they are once that paragraph exists. Optional: rename figure titles to “Attested Enrollment (EST Server contacts the Verifier)” if “Passport” in a caption still causes trouble.

issues.title: Cite TACRA for Freshness Kind names; stop calling every request `handle` a Freshness Handle
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Grok has flagged the following Important issue in the draft and suggested a solution:

Terminology currently points the five kinds and `handle` at the wrong documents:

```
* Freshness Kind: … `absent-timestamp`, `absent-none`, `absent-epoch`,
  `present-nonce`, or `present-epoch` ({{INTERACTION-MODELS}}, Section 10 of {{RFC9334}})
* Freshness Handle: freshness element included in Evidence when Freshness Kind
  is not `absent-none` ({{INTERACTION-MODELS}})
```

RFC 9334 §10 has timestamp, nonce, and epoch. INTERACTION-MODELS has Handle. Neither defines `absent-timestamp`, `present-nonce`, or the other three tokens. Those names are TACRA `{#freshness-kind}`.

The same glossary entry then equates **Freshness Handle** with **freshness element**. TACRA splits them:

- Freshness Handle: value returned by Initiate for `present-nonce` / `present-epoch`.
- Freshness element: what the binding digest covers — Handle, 8-octet timestamp, epoch marker, or empty.

Wire CDDL already follows TACRA: initiate `handle` only for `present-*`; second-leg `handle` for every kind except `absent-none`. The prose does not:

- Initiate field: “Freshness Handle — REQUIRED for `present-nonce` and `present-epoch`.” Correct.
- Enroll/retrieve field: “Freshness Handle — REQUIRED when `freshness_kind` is not `absent-none`. MUST equal the Handle returned by `attest-initiate` when present.” For `absent-timestamp` / `absent-epoch` nothing was returned, so “Handle” and “MUST equal the Handle” do not apply.
- Field bullets for `absent-timestamp` still cite RFC 9334 §10.1 instead of TACRA.

Security Considerations repeats the mix (“a nonce Handle … a timestamp … an epoch marker … (Section 10 of RFC 9334)”).

Readers (and an RP recomputing the digest) cannot tell whether second-leg `handle` is the initiate Handle, a timestamp, or a local epoch marker.

**Suggested solution**

Point the five names at TACRA. Keep the JSON member `handle`. Describe initiate `handle` as a Freshness Handle and second-leg `handle` as the freshness element. Concrete edits:

Glossary:

```md
* Freshness Kind: the recency method; one of `absent-timestamp`, `absent-none`,
  `absent-epoch`, `present-nonce`, or `present-epoch` ({{TACRA}})
* Freshness Handle: the value `attest-initiate` returns for `present-nonce` and
  `present-epoch` ({{TACRA}}, {{INTERACTION-MODELS}})
* Freshness element: the octets the binding digest covers ({{TACRA}}): the
  Freshness Handle, the Attester's timestamp, a locally held epoch marker, or
  empty for `absent-none`. On `attest-enroll` and `attest-retrieve` this is the
  `handle` member when present.
```

`{{initiation-response}}` `freshness_kind` bullets: cite `{{TACRA}}` for each kind; keep RFC 9334 §10 only as the general freshness discussion.

Enrollment and retrieval `handle` bullets (same text both places):

```md
* handle (bytes): freshness element — REQUIRED when `freshness_kind` is not
  `absent-none`; MUST be absent otherwise.
  For `present-nonce` and `present-epoch` it MUST equal the Freshness Handle
  returned by `attest-initiate`.
  For `absent-timestamp` it is the 8-octet big-endian Unix timestamp.
  For `absent-epoch` it is the locally held epoch marker.
```

(The two encodings match critical #2 / `{#est-binding}` if that section is added; otherwise state them here.)

Security Considerations freshness bullet: cite `{{TACRA}}` for kinds and element; RFC 9334 §10 for the three recency methods in general.

Optional: carry TACRA’s Handle lifetime guidance (SHOULD NOT be below 60 seconds) on initiate `expires_in`, or say this profile chooses otherwise.

issues.title: CSR-ATTEST is extra key-property Evidence; put that rule in TACRA and point EST at it
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Grok has flagged the following Important issue and suggested a solution for it.

EST `{{relationship}}` currently:

```md
{{CSR-ATTEST}} conveys Evidence inside the CSR, in its `id-aa-attestation` attribute.
It makes the CA/RA responsible for validating the binding between the attestations
and the CSR's public key (Section 6.1 of {{CSR-ATTEST}}).
This document conveys Evidence beside the CSR … the Evidence is produced over a
digest that includes the finished CSR, so it cannot travel inside it.
Placing attestations in the CSR as well … is an optional interoperability path
for an Attester whose platform can make claims about the CSR key
```

Problems:

- The TACRA-binding Evidence **cannot** be that CSR attribute. The digest covers the finished CSR (plus freshness and Target). Putting that Evidence inside the CSR is circular. The “optional path” is therefore a **second** attestation, not the same object. Neither draft says that clearly.
- CSR-ATTEST `-32` §6.1 no longer means “CA binds attestations to the CSR public key” in the old sense. It says a public key (or its hash) in platform Evidence does **not**, by itself, prove the private key was generated or is protected in the attested environment. Citing §6.1 as if it were the TACRA digest, then offering CSR-ATTEST “as well” for “claims about the CSR key,” can be read as replacing TACRA’s binding.
- That caveat is an **architecture** claim (digest-of-CSR ≠ CSKpri generated in the TEE). It belongs in TACRA. If only EST paraphrases §6.1, EST goes stale when CSR-ATTEST revvs.

Do **not** change TACRA’s Enrollment subject from the finished CSR to the CSR public key so Evidence can ride in `id-aa-attestation`. That would let the CAS rewrite SAN/subject/extensions around the same key and would drop TACRA’s untrusted-CAS property.

**Suggested solution**

Keep the digest over the DER CSR. State the CSR-ATTEST rule once in TACRA. Make EST a short profile of that text.

**TACRA `{#binding}`** — add, do not retarget the digest:

```md
The Enrollment subject is the DER-encoded CSR. Evidence that carries this
digest therefore cannot appear in that CSR, including as the `id-aa-attestation`
attribute of {{CSR-ATTEST}}. {{CSR-ATTEST}} does not replace this binding.

{{CSR-ATTEST}} MAY carry additional attestations about the CSR key (for example
that CSKpri was generated in the attested environment). This digest does not
prove that. When a Credential Authority relies on such attestations, Section 6.1
of {{CSR-ATTEST}} applies: a public key or its hash in platform Evidence does
not, by itself, demonstrate that the corresponding private key was generated or
is protected in the attested environment.
```

**EST `{{relationship}}`** — replace the CSR-ATTEST paragraphs with a pointer:

```md
{{CSR-ATTEST}} conveys attestations inside the CSR. This profile conveys the
TACRA binding Evidence beside the CSR, in AttestedEnrollmentRequest
({{enrollment-request}}), as {{TACRA}} requires: that Evidence's freshness
input covers the finished CSR, so it cannot travel inside it.

Evidence beside the CSR is mandatory. Additional {{CSR-ATTEST}} attributes in
the CSR are optional, for key-property claims this profile's digest does not
prove, under the rules of {{TACRA}} and of Section 6.1 of {{CSR-ATTEST}}.
Whether a Credential Authority requires that path is agreed out of band.
Retrieval has no CSR and binds Evidence to CEKpub ({{evidence-to-cek}}).
```

Do not put the TACRA-binding Evidence in `id-aa-attestation`. If a CA requires CSR-ATTEST, it is extra Evidence, appraised under CSR-ATTEST §6.1, not a second copy of the binding digest.

One thing kept: the citation of Section 6.1 is accurate in revision 32, which makes the CA/RA responsible for ensuring that the binding has been validated, the sentence the profile cites, and carries the caveat about a public key in platform Evidence in the same section.

issues.title: `attest-initiate` is not `/nonce`: size, association, and “Handle = freshness nonce” are unspecified
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Grok has flagged this Important issue and has suggested a solution for it:

`{{relationship}}` currently:

```md
`attest-initiate` covers the same first leg for the `present-nonce` Freshness Kind
and, in addition, returns the Freshness Kind, the Credential Acquisition Mode and
the acceptable CSK or CEK algorithms, none of which the nonce resource carries.
A `present-nonce` Handle is a nonce in the sense of {{ATTESTATION-FRESHNESS}},
and the requirement of Section 5.1 of that document that the server associate
the nonce with the subsequent request applies to `attest-initiate` and its
second leg alike.
An EST Server MAY offer both resources.
```

That over-identifies the two resources.

**Size and entropy.** Freshness `-09` §5.1: nonce is 8–64 bytes, ≥64 bits of entropy, unique, not reused. This profile never constrains `handle`. A 4-byte Handle, or a Handle that is not fresh random, is not a nonce in that sense. TEE REPORT_DATA is 64 octets, but that field holds the **digest**, not the Handle.

**No `len`.** Freshness GET is parameterless; POST carries `len` (and optional type info) so the Attester can ask for a platform-sized nonce. `attest-initiate` has `target` and `credential_type` and no length. An Attester that needs 32 vs 64 bytes of Handle cannot say so.

**Association is not the same mechanism.** Freshness §5.1 binds nonce request to the later CSR with TLS session (or cookies). This profile also correlates `handle` with initiate `target` / `credential_type` (409/403) and TACRA puts the Handle in the binding digest. Saying “§5.1 applies alike” hides that extra correlation and does not say whether TLS session is required on top.

**`expires_in` vs `expiry`.** Same quantity (seconds), different names. Unstated.

**Two resources.** “MAY offer both” does not say whether a `/nonce` value may be reused as an `attest-initiate` Handle (or the reverse). They are not substitutes: `/nonce` does not return kind, mode, or algorithms, and enroll/retrieve need those plus the digest.

**GET that mints a single-use Handle** is the same RFC 9110 compromise Freshness `-09` already makes for GET `/nonce`. Worth one sentence, not a redesign.

TACRA today: Handle lifetime SHOULD NOT be below 60 seconds; CAS MUST NOT mint `present-nonce`; no size, entropy, or length-request on Initiate-Credential-Acquisition.

**Suggested solution**

Do not claim a Handle **is** a freshness nonce until both drafts say it is one. Keep two resources; define `present-nonce` Handles so EST can use them with `/nonce`’s rules; do not mix the two URLs.

**TACRA `{#freshness-kind}` / Initiate**

```md
A `present-nonce` Freshness Handle is a nonce: it MUST contain at least 64 bits
of entropy, MUST be unique, and MUST NOT be reused (Section 10.2 of {{RFC9334}}).
Its length is between 8 and 64 octets inclusive, as {{ATTESTATION-FRESHNESS}}
requires for EST/CMP/CMC nonces.

Initiate-Credential-Acquisition MAY take a requested length in that range.
The originator returns a Handle of that length, or the length its policy sets
if none was requested.

A Freshness Handle originator SHOULD NOT set a lifetime below 60 seconds.
```

(Lifetime sentence is already there; keep it.)

Do **not** put TLS-session association in TACRA. The Attester has no network. Association at the architecture layer is: the party that issued the Handle checks it, and the RP recomputes the digest that includes it.

**EST `{{relationship}}`** — replace the three sentences with:

```md
{{ATTESTATION-FRESHNESS}} defines `/.well-known/est/nonce` (GET, or POST with
`application/est-attestation-freshness+json`). The response carries a `nonce`
of 8 to 64 bytes and an OPTIONAL `expiry` in seconds (Section 5.1).

For the `present-nonce` Freshness Kind, `attest-initiate` is the first leg that
returns that nonce, as a Freshness Handle, plus the Freshness Kind, the
Credential Acquisition Mode, and the acceptable CSK or CEK algorithms
({{initiation-response}}), none of which `/nonce` carries.

A `present-nonce` Handle in this profile is a nonce as {{TACRA}} and
Section 5.1 of {{ATTESTATION-FRESHNESS}} specify (8 to 64 bytes, ≥64 bits of
entropy, unique, not reused). `expires_in` is that document's `expiry`: seconds
until the originator no longer accepts the Handle.

Section 5.1's requirement that the server associate the nonce with the
subsequent request applies. This profile does that by (1) the TLS session or
cookies of Section 5.1, (2) correlating `handle` with the `target` and
`credential_type` of the `attest-initiate` that returned it, and (3) the
Relying Party recomputing the digest of {{TACRA}} that includes the Handle.

An EST Server MAY offer both `/nonce` and `attest-initiate`. They are not
interchangeable. A client that will call `attest-enroll` or `attest-retrieve`
MUST obtain the Handle from `attest-initiate` (or complete initiate locally
for an `absent-*` kind). A nonce obtained from `/nonce` MUST NOT be sent as
`handle` on those resources unless the server has stated that the two URLs
share Handle state, which this document does not require.
```

**EST `attest-initiate`**

- Optional query parameter `len`: requested Handle length in bytes, 8..64, only meaningful when the response kind will be `present-nonce`. Server ignores it for other kinds.
- `expires_in`: same meaning as freshness `expiry`.
- One sentence: GET that mints a single-use Handle has the same side effect as GET `/nonce` in {{ATTESTATION-FRESHNESS}}; the Handle is bound as in `{{relationship}}`.

No change to POST vs GET for `-00` unless you want full alignment with freshness POST; query `len` is enough.

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: Done in #31 and TheBankster/rats-tacra#27: a present-nonce Handle is 8 to 64 octets, at least 64 bits of entropy, issued once and not reused, in the CDDL and in prose; expires_in is named as the freshness draft's expiry; the two resources are told apart. Two of the suggestions do not fit the architecture, and the text says why: no requested length, since the Handle enters the Evidence through the digest and no platform needs a Handle of a particular size (the bench's are 32 octets); no TLS session or cookie for the association, since either would bind the EST Client, the conduit, not the Attester.

issues.title: EST Server 403 on `credential_type` is not authorization; TACRA type/hint stay unbound
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Grok has flagged the following Important issue and suggested a solution for it.

Architecture says the EST Client and EST Server have no RATS role and **MUST NOT authorize** issuance or release.

Enrollment/retrieval processing then has the EST Server refuse the second leg with **403 Forbidden** when `target`, `freshness_kind`, or `credential_type` (when carried) differ from the `attest-initiate` that returned the Handle. Error Handling uses the same 403 for that mismatch **and** for “attestation failed” / “policy denies enrollment/retrieval.”

TACRA `{#untrusted-cas}`: the CAS is a conduit. **Credential Type and Credential Hint are not in the binding.** The RATS Relying Party’s policy, not the CAS, caps what is minted or released. The RP **MUST take the Freshness Kind for a Target from its own policy, not from the request.** Target **is** in the digest, so a substituted Target fails at the RP even if the CAS forwards it.

So:

- EST Server 403 when second-leg `credential_type` ≠ initiate’s type treats the CAS copy of type as authoritative. That is appraisal of an unbound field. A malicious EST Server can skip the check and forward anyway; the 403 is not a control against untrusted CAS.
- Bundling that 403 with “policy denies” / “attestation failed” makes a session mismatch look like an RP decision.
- Correlating `handle` with `target` (and with the kind **initiate returned**) is useful session hygiene so two in-flight exchanges are not mixed. It is not authorization. The RP still recomputes the digest (Target) and still applies its own Freshness Kind policy.

Hint is already described as non-authorizing in the EST glossary; it is not in the 403 list. Type should be treated the same way.

**Suggested solution**

Keep Handle↔Target correlation. Stop treating type (and request `freshness_kind`) as EST Server policy. Say once in TACRA that type/hint are unbound; EST only implements session correlation and forwards RP 403s.

**TACRA** (untrusted CAS / binding — make the profile rule explicit):

```md
Credential Type and Credential Hint are not in the binding. The CAS MAY
forward them. The RATS Relying Party MUST apply its own policy to the type
and the hint and MUST NOT treat the CAS's copies as authorizing issuance or
release.

The Relying Party MUST take the Freshness Kind for a Target from its own
policy, not from the request. The Target is in the binding; a CAS that
substitutes a Target fails the digest check.

A Credential Acquisition Mechanism MAY correlate a Freshness Handle with the
Target (and with the Freshness Kind returned for that Handle) so that two
in-flight exchanges are not mixed. That correlation is session hygiene. It
is not appraisal and does not replace the Relying Party's checks.
```

**EST — processing step 2** (enroll and retrieve, same idea):

```md
2. For `present-nonce` and `present-epoch`, correlate `handle` with the
   `attest-initiate` that returned it:
   * 409 Conflict when no `attest-initiate` returned this Handle or it has
     expired; a `present-nonce` Handle is single-use;
   * 403 Forbidden when the request `target` differs from that
     `attest-initiate`'s, or when request `freshness_kind` differs from the
     kind that `attest-initiate` returned.

   This correlation is session hygiene ({{TACRA}}). It is not authorization.
   The EST Server MUST still forward a well-formed request that passes it.
   The Credential Authority or Secret Vault takes Freshness Kind from its
   policy for the Target, recomputes the digest, and authorizes issuance or
   release.

   `credential_type` and `credential_hint` are not correlated. The EST Server
   forwards them; the Relying Party MAY use them, ignore them, or deny with
   403 Forbidden.

   For `absent-*` kinds no Handle was returned. The Relying Party checks the
   freshness element under the Freshness Kind its policy sets for the Target.
```

**EST — Error Handling 403**, split the CAS case from the RP case:

```md
* 403 Forbidden:
  * from the EST Server: it does not serve the `target` of `attest-initiate`
    (or that `credential_type` on initiate, when asking for the first-leg
    mode); or, on the second leg, `target` or `freshness_kind` differ from
    the `attest-initiate` that returned this Handle (session correlation);
  * forwarded from the RATS Relying Party: attestation failed, or policy
    denies enrollment or retrieval (including type or hint the RP will not
    honor).
```

Initiate 403 “does not serve that Target, or that `credential_type` for it” can stay: that is “this EST Server has no configured mode for that pair,” not second-leg authorization.

**EST — Architecture restrictions:** keep MUST NOT authorize. Add one sentence: correlating a Handle with Target/kind does not count as authorizing; denying on type/hint does, and is the RP’s job.

No change to the binding construction. Type and hint stay out of the digest.

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: Done in #31 and TheBankster/rats-tacra#27: the correlation named as the EST Server keeping its two legs together, not authorization; the 403 list split into the EST Server's own refusals and the forwarded ones; one sentence in TACRA's Trust Model, which already said that the type and the hint travel unbound and the Relying Party's policy decides. credential_type stays among the correlated members, as the code correlates it; your call to drop it.

issues.title: Security Considerations omit Evidence/AR on the CAS path, channel binding, privacy, and EST client authentication
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Grok has flagged the following Important issue and suggested a solution for it:

`{{security}}` covers key substitution, over-issuance, shared replica keys, freshness, the EST Server→Verifier channel, size/rate limits, and not swapping in classic EST. It does not cover the TACRA threat model this profile instantiates.

Missing, all already in (or implied by) TACRA / RFC 9334:

**Evidence and Attestation Results on the CAS path.** Goal 10 hides **secrets** from the CAS. Evidence and AR are not secrets. They travel as JSON/bytes through EST Client and EST Server (RFC 9334 §12.2). The draft never says that. Enrollment returns a cert in plaintext (public); retrieval ciphertext is opaque — that split is unstated in Security Considerations.

**No channel binding.** TACRA’s digest is freshness || Target || CSR/CEKpub. It has no Relying Party identifier and no TLS exporter. A relay on the EST path can forward a live exchange to another Credential Authority or Secret Vault that serves the **same Target name**. TACRA `{#untrusted-cas}` discusses RP substitution; EST does not. The Attester has no network (Goal 8), so it cannot bind to the EST Client↔Server TLS session unless the exporter is passed into the Attesting Environment. That is an architecture gap, not an EST-only omission.

**Privacy.** Evidence often carries device/firmware identifiers (RFC 9334 §11). They are visible to EST Client, EST Server, Verifier, and RP. No Privacy Considerations.

**Who may call `attest-*`.** RFC 7030 requires client authentication for `/simpleenroll`. This profile never says whether `attest-initiate` / `attest-enroll` / `attest-retrieve` do. An unauthenticated GET that mints `present-nonce` Handles is Handle exhaustion / DoS. globalsign-est uses mTLS on the TACRA backend; the draft does not. TACRA `{#cas-client-auth}` leaves CAS Client authentication to **profiles**. This document is that profile and is silent.

**EST Server → RP.** Only the Verifier channel is required to provide integrity/authenticity/replay protection. The path to the Credential Authority / Secret Vault is unstated (AR or Evidence on that hop).

Type/hint unbound is Important #5; do not duplicate it here beyond a pointer.

**Suggested solution**

Put architecture threats in TACRA once. EST states the EST mapping (who sees what, client auth, initiate rate limits) and does **not** add a TLS exporter to the digest unless you deliberately drop or qualify Goal 8.

**TACRA Security Considerations** — add if not already this explicit:

```md
Evidence and Attestation Results are visible to the CAS Client and CAS Server
(Section 12.2 of {{RFC9334}}). Goal 10 applies to retrieved secrets and to
CSKpri, not to Evidence, AR, or public certificates.

The binding ({{binding}}) does not include a Relying Party identifier or a
channel binding (for example a TLS exporter {{RFC9266}}). A CAS that relays
an exchange to a different Credential Authority or Secret Vault that serves
the same Target can still satisfy the digest. Deployments that need to pin
the RP do so by configuration of the CAS Server (which RPs it may contact),
not by the digest. Binding the EST/CAS TLS session would require the
Attesting Environment to learn a channel binding from the CAS Client, which
this architecture does not assume (Goal 8).

Evidence may contain identifiers that fingerprint a device or workload
(Section 11 of {{RFC9334}}).

Authentication of the CAS Client to the CAS Server, and of the CAS Server to
the Verifier and RATS Relying Party, is specified by the Credential
Acquisition Mechanism profile. This document requires integrity, authenticity,
and replay protection on those hops; it does not require a particular method.
```

Keep `{#untrusted-cas}` as the RP-substitution discussion; the paragraph above is the pointer from Security Considerations.

**Do not** add the TLS exporter to `binding_input` for `-00`. That is a new binding version and needs the exporter inside the TEE.

**EST `{{security}}` — Common to Both Modes**, keep the existing bullets and add:

```md
* Evidence and Attestation Results: the EST Client and EST Server see Evidence
  and, in Passport mode, Attestation Results, in plaintext (Section 12.2 of
  {{RFC9334}}, {{TACRA}}). Retrieved secrets stay in EncryptedCredentialBundle
  ({{bundle}}). Newly enrolled certificates are public and returned as
  simpleenroll. CSKpri and CEKpri MUST NOT leave the Attester.

* Channel binding: the digest of {{TACRA}} does not bind the exchange to the
  EST TLS session or to a particular Credential Authority or Secret Vault.
  A relay that preserves Target, freshness element, and CSR/CEKpub still
  verifies. Which RP the EST Server contacts is a deployment choice of the
  EST Server. This profile does not require a TLS exporter in Evidence.

* Privacy: Evidence may fingerprint the Attester (Section 11 of {{RFC9334}}).
  Error bodies MUST NOT echo Evidence or Attestation Results (already under
  Error Handling).

* EST client authentication: `attest-enroll` and `attest-retrieve` follow
  Section 3.3.2 of {{RFC7030}} (client authentication as for simpleenroll).
  `attest-initiate` MAY be offered without client authentication; an EST
  Server that mints `present-nonce` Handles on unauthenticated GET MUST rate-
  limit and cap outstanding Handles per source (DoS / Handle exhaustion).
  Deployments MAY require TLS client certificates on all three resources.

* Channels: the EST Server's channels to the Verifier and to the Credential
  Authority or Secret Vault MUST provide integrity, authenticity, and replay
  protection (replace the Verifier-only bullet).

* Classic EST: keep the existing MUST NOT substitute classic EST for an
  attested request.

* Type and hint: unbound; see {{TACRA}} and the processing rules (Important #5).
```

**EST Architecture or `{{attest-initiate}}`:** one sentence that client auth for initiate is OPTIONAL, for enroll/retrieve REQUIRED as simpleenroll, unless the deployment’s EST policy is stronger (mTLS on all three).

**Privacy:** either a short `## Privacy Considerations` that points at RFC 9334 §11 and the Evidence-on-CAS-path bullet, or fold it into Common as above. A separate section is easier for RATS reviewers.

No IANA or CDDL change. No binding-construction change unless you later specify an optional `method` that includes a channel binding passed in through CAAPI.

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: Done in #31: Evidence and Attestation Results on the conduit's path, channel binding (none, by Design Goal 8, and TACRA's Trust Model says what a relay to another Relying Party obtains), client authentication (none required for attest-*, a deployment may require it as for simpleenroll, rate limits on Handles minted on an unauthenticated initiate), both channels of the EST Server, the unbound type and hint, and a Privacy Considerations section. TACRA (TheBankster/rats-tacra#27) gains the channel-binding sentence in its Trust Model, where the rest already was. No TLS exporter in the digest, as you say.

issues.title: `group_id` hashes an unbound `credential_hint` and never names H
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Grok has flagged the following Important issue and suggested a solution for it:

Retrieval currently:

```md
The Secret Vault MUST map Attestation Results to a credential group ID that is
stable for replica workloads and distinct across security domains, tenants, and
credential selections.

A typical construction is:

group_id = H(attestation_subject || credential_hint || policy_version)

Where attestation_subject is derived from Attestation Results (not raw Evidence)
to avoid nonce/freshness variability.
```

Problems:

- **`credential_hint` is unbound** (TACRA `{#untrusted-cas}`, EST glossary: the Vault MAY use, ignore, or reject it). Putting the raw request hint in `group_id` lets the CAS or Attester change which vault slot is selected by rewriting the hint. That can enlarge the set of secrets a given AR can reach (confused deputy) or split replicas that should share a group.
- **`H` is unnamed.** SHA-256 vs SHA-512 vs HMAC vs “whatever” is not interoperable if two Vaults must compute the same id.
- **Concatenation has no length prefixes.** TACRA’s binding uses `len32` for that reason. `attestation_subject` and `policy_version` encodings are unspecified, so even a named H would not be stable.
- The paragraph is labeled “typical construction” but sits under a MUST that the Vault map AR to a group id. Readers will treat the formula as the mapping.

TACRA today: replica workloads share credentials; the Vault MAY use the hint to **locate** a credential. It does not define `group_id` and does not say the hint MUST NOT enlarge the set that AR+policy already allows.

Bundle AAD authenticating `credential_hint` (critical #1) is a different issue: that binds the hint that was **sent**, it does not use the hint as a group key.

**3) Suggested solution**

`group_id` is Vault policy, not an EST wire algorithm. Select the group from Attestation Results and Vault policy only. Use the hint, if at all, as a selector **inside** that set. Name this once in TACRA; EST drops the MUST-formula.

**TACRA** (Retrieval / Secret Vault):

```md
The Secret Vault maps Attestation Results to a credential group that is stable
for replica workloads and distinct across security domains, tenants, and the
Vault's credential selections. That mapping is the Vault's policy. This
document does not specify the identifier's syntax.

A Credential Hint MAY select among credentials that mapping already allows.
It MUST NOT enlarge that set. The CAS cannot select a group by rewriting the
hint; a hint the policy does not recognize is ignored or the request is denied.
```

**EST — replace “Credential Group ID Determination”:**

```md
### Credential Group ID Determination {#group-id}

The Secret Vault maps Attestation Results to a `group_id` as {{TACRA}}
requires: stable for replica workloads, distinct across security domains,
tenants, and the Vault's credential selections. The identifier is the Vault's
policy. This profile does not require a particular construction and does not
require two Vaults to compute the same value.

`credential_hint` MUST NOT be an input to that mapping. The Vault MAY use the
hint only to choose among credentials `group_id` already allows, or it MAY
ignore the hint, or it MAY deny the request with 403 Forbidden.

An example (not a requirement) of a mapping that does not take the hint is:

  group_id = SHA-256( len32(attestation_subject) || attestation_subject
                    || len32(policy_version)      || policy_version )

where `attestation_subject` is a Vault-chosen octet string derived from
Attestation Results (not raw Evidence, so freshness does not churn the group)
and `policy_version` is a Vault-chosen octet string that names the release
policy. `len32` is as in {{TACRA}}.
```

Processing step 4 can stay “computes `group_id`”; it now means “applies `{#group-id}`,” not the old hash.

If `{#bundle}` AAD includes `credential_hint`, that authenticates the hint **on that response**. It does not put the hint in `group_id`. Keep those roles separate.

No CDDL change unless `group_id` is already a text field of the bundle (it should remain an opaque string the Vault mints).

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: Done in #31 and TheBankster/rats-tacra#27: the group is the Secret Vault's policy, no construction specified, the hint selects within what the policy allows and cannot enlarge it, the formula with the hint gone. One difference from the suggestion: the hint may select among the credentials the policy allows, which is what the bench's Vault does (Target and hint name the group, the policy bounds the set), rather than being forbidden as an input altogether; the security property is the same.

issues.title: IANA: drop unspecified identifier registries; fix change controller, contact, and algorithm tokens
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Grok has flagged the following Important issue and suggested a solution for it:

`{{iana}}` currently:

- Correctly does **not** request an EST path registry (`attest-*` are additional services under RFC 7030 §3.2.2).
- Requests media types for the `attest-*` JSON messages (templates are close to RFC 6838).
- Then: “This document also requests a registry of acceptable_evidence identifiers and credential_type identifiers (if not reused from existing registries).”

That last sentence is not a registry request. There is no registry name, allocation policy (FCFS / Expert Review / Specification Required), registration template, or initial contents. IANA and the IESG will bounce it. Critical #3 already proposes in-document `credential_type` tokens instead of a registry.

Media-type template nits:

- **Change controller** is `IETF`. RFC 7030 and usual IETF media types use **IESG**.
- **Person to contact** is “IETF LAMPS Working Group (spasm@ietf.org)” on an **unadopted individual** Informational draft. RFC 6838 wants a person; until LAMPS adopts this, use an author.

`acceptable_csk` / `acceptable_cek` are arrays of unconstrained `text` in CDDL. No format (COSE alg, JWA, OID, HPKE suite string). globalsign-est uses `ecdsa-p256-sha256` and `ECDH-P256+HKDF-SHA256+A256GCM`. Two implementations cannot advertise a suite.

`acceptable_evidence` / `profile` have the same hole (also Important #11). Do not invent a registry to paper over missing tokens.

Registering `application/est-attest-bundle+json` while `{{bundle}}` is still a TODO is Critical #1, not this issue.

TACRA has no IANA section for these tokens. A shared “Credential Type” registry across mechanisms would live in TACRA, not here. Neither draft should request it in `-00`.

**Suggested solution**

For `-00`: register only the media types whose payloads are defined. Define CSK/CEK/evidence/type **tokens in the document**. No new registries. Align the media-type boilerplate with RFC 7030.

**TACRA:** do not add IANA registries for Credential Type or Evidence format. Keep types as prose (X.509, WIC, WIT, JWT, …). If a later WG document wants a registry, that is a TACRA (or WIMSE) document with a real policy, not a one-liner in this EST profile.

**EST `{#iana}`** — replace the registry sentence and fix the templates:

```md
# IANA Considerations {#iana}

The `attest-*` resources are additional services of an EST server
(Section 3.2.2 of {{RFC7030}}), under the well-known URI suffix "est"
that {{RFC7030}} registered. No registry of EST operation paths exists,
so none is requested.

IANA is requested to register the media types of {{media-types}} in the
"Media Types" registry {{RFC6838}}.

This document does not request registries for `credential_type`,
`acceptable_evidence`, `acceptable_csk`, or `acceptable_cek`. Those values
are protocol tokens defined in this document ({{credential-type}},
{{alg-tokens}}).
```

In **every** media-type registration:

```md
Person & email address to contact for further information:
: Serhii Nikolaichuk <nikolaichuk.s.f@gmail.com>

Change controller:
: IESG
```

(Use whichever author should own IANA mail; not `spasm@ietf.org` until the WG adopts the draft.)

If `{#bundle}` is still undefined, omit `application/est-attest-bundle+json` from the request (Critical #1).

**EST — algorithm / evidence tokens** (new short section, referenced from IANA and from `{{initiation-response}}`):

```md
## Protocol tokens {#alg-tokens}

`acceptable_csk` and `acceptable_cek` are arrays of ASCII tokens.

This profile's mandatory CSK token is:

* `ecdsa-p256-sha256`: ECDSA on NIST P-256 with SHA-256 (CSK for Enrollment)

This profile's mandatory CEK token is:

* `HPKE-Base-P256-SHA256-A256GCM`: HPKE Base with DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256),
  HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM ({{RFC9180}}, {{bundle}})

An EST Server that returns `mode` `enroll` MUST include `ecdsa-p256-sha256`
in `acceptable_csk`. One that returns `retrieve` MUST include
`HPKE-Base-P256-SHA256-A256GCM` in `acceptable_cek`. Other tokens are
out of scope for this version; a client MUST NOT use a token not listed
in the `attest-initiate` response.

`acceptable_evidence` / `profile`, when present, are ASCII tokens naming
an Evidence format. This version does not define a token; if the array is
omitted, `profile` on the second leg is omitted and the Relying Party
accepts the Evidence formats its policy allows for the Target.
```

(`credential_type` tokens stay in `{#credential-type}` from Critical #3.)

**CDDL:** keep `[+ text]` for the arrays; the prose above is the profile constraint. Optionally:

```cddl
acceptable_csk = [+ tstr]
acceptable_cek = [+ tstr]
```

No Expert Review, no “TBD registry.” Revisit a registry only if LAMPS wants other suites to be added without a new RFC.

issues.title: `attest-*` paths omit RFC 7030’s optional extra path segment (`/.well-known/est/<label>/`)
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Grok has flagged the following Important issue and has suggested a solution for it.

Protocol Overview lists only:

```
/.well-known/est/attest-initiate
/.well-known/est/attest-enroll
/.well-known/est/attest-retrieve
```

RFC 7030 §3.2.2: an EST server **MAY** insert an extra path segment between `est` and the operation (`/.well-known/est/<label>/simpleenroll`) so one host can serve several CAs. The label MUST NOT collide with an operation name. The server MUST still serve the unlabeled URLs.

`attest-initiate`, `attest-enroll`, and `attest-retrieve` are additional operations in that same tree (IANA already says so). They need the same rule. As written, a client that already talks to `/.well-known/est/tenant-a/simpleenroll` has no specified place for `attest-*`.

globalsign-est already implements this (`aps`). The draft does not.

Do not conflate `<label>` with TACRA **Target**. Target is the RATS-unaware Relying Party the Attester wants credentials **for** (query/body `target`). The EST label selects which EST issuer / front-end on that host (which Credential Authority or Secret Vault the EST Server is configured to use). A deployment MAY use one label per Target; this profile must not require that.

`attest-initiate` / `attest-enroll` / `attest-retrieve` as labels would be illegal under RFC 7030 (collision with operation names).

TACRA has no HTTP paths. Multiplexing several RPs on one CAS Server is a mechanism detail.

**Suggested solution**

State RFC 7030 labels once in EST. Keep Target as the TACRA field. Optional one-liner in TACRA that profiles MAY multiplex RPs with mechanism-specific names.

**EST — Protocol Overview:**

```md
Three new EST operations are added under the existing EST well-known prefix
(Section 3.2.2 of {{RFC7030}}):

* `attest-initiate`
* `attest-enroll`
* `attest-retrieve`

They sit next to `/cacerts`, `/simpleenroll`, and the other RFC 7030 operations.
An EST Server that uses the optional extra path segment of Section 3.2.2
(for example `/.well-known/est/arbitraryLabel1/simpleenroll`) MUST offer the
`attest-*` operations under that same prefix:

* `/.well-known/est/attest-initiate`
* `/.well-known/est/<label>/attest-initiate`

and likewise for `attest-enroll` and `attest-retrieve`.
The label MUST NOT be `attest-initiate`, `attest-enroll`, or `attest-retrieve`.

The extra path segment selects an EST issuer configuration (which Credential
Authority or Secret Vault that EST Server uses). It is not the TACRA Target.
The Target remains the `target` query parameter or JSON member ({{TACRA}}).
A client uses the same `<label>` for `attest-*` that it uses for `/simpleenroll`
on that issuer.
```

**EST — `{#iana}`:** keep “no path registry.” Add: the optional label is RFC 7030’s, not a new registration; the new operation names are `attest-initiate`, `attest-enroll`, `attest-retrieve`.

**EST — `attest-initiate`:** no change to query parameters. Label is in the URL path, not in `target`.

**TACRA** (CAS / mechanism profile, optional):

```md
A Credential Acquisition Mechanism MAY multiplex several Credential Authorities
or Secret Vaults on one CAS Server using mechanism-specific names (for EST, the
optional extra path segment of Section 3.2.2 of {{RFC7030}}). Those names are
not the Target. The Target is the RATS-unaware Relying Party the Attester
seeks credentials for.
```

No CDDL or media-type change. Examples, if added (Important #10), should show both `/.well-known/est/attest-initiate?target=...` and `/.well-known/est/label1/attest-initiate?target=...`.

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body: Done in #31 and TheBankster/rats-tacra#27: the attest-* operations offered under the optional path segment of RFC 7030 as well, the segment selecting the issuer and never the Target.

issues.title: Add HTTP examples for `attest-initiate`, `attest-enroll`, and `attest-retrieve`
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Grok has flagged the following Important issue and has suggested a solution for it:

The draft has no examples: no HTTP exchanges, no JSON payloads, no `curl`. RFC 7030 Appendix A, `draft-ietf-lamps-attestation-freshness-09`, and the globalsign-est README all show request/response pairs. Implementers cannot check CDDL, query parameters, or media types against a worked message.

What is missing, in particular:

- GET `attest-initiate` with required `target` and optional `credential_type` (URI-encoded).
- 200 `AttestationInitiationResponse` for enroll vs retrieve (`present-nonce` with `handle` / `expires_in` vs `absent-*` with no handle).
- 400 (no `target`) and 403 (unknown Target).
- POST `attest-enroll` / `attest-retrieve` with `Content-Type`, `handle` as freshness element, `binding`, truncated `csr` / `evidence` / `cek_pub`.
- Success: PKCS#7 certs-only for enroll; bundle JSON for retrieve (once Critical #1 defines it).
- Optional RFC 7030 extra path segment (Important #9): one URL with `<label>`.

globalsign-est’s `curl` uses `/api/v1/attestation/initiate`, not `/.well-known/est/…`. Do not copy that path into this document.

TACRA is architecture (commands, not HTTP). Examples belong in this EST profile. No TACRA change required beyond keeping Target / kind / Handle names aligned.

**3) Suggested solution**

Add an informative appendix. Use RFC 7030-style hosts (`est.example.com`), truncated base64url, and a note that payloads are illustrative. One complete initiate exchange is worth more than three incomplete ones. Fill enroll/retrieve bodies with placeholders until `{#est-binding}` and `{#bundle}` land; then replace the placeholders.

**New appendix:**

```md
# Appendix A. Example Messages {#examples}

These examples are informative. Line wrapping and truncated base64url
values are for readability. Evidence, CSRs, and HPKE ciphertexts are
not valid platform artifacts.

## A.1. attest-initiate (enroll, present-nonce)

GET /.well-known/est/attest-initiate?target=https%3A%2F%2Fca.example.com%2Fworkloads&credential_type=x509 HTTP/1.1
Host: est.example.com
Accept: application/est-attest-initiate+json

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/est-attest-initiate+json

{
  "freshness_kind": "present-nonce",
  "handle": "VGhpc0lzQVByZXNlbnROb25jZUhhbmRsZQ",
  "expires_in": 600,
  "mode": "enroll",
  "acceptable_csk": ["ecdsa-p256-sha256"]
}

The same operation under an RFC 7030 extra path segment:

GET /.well-known/est/tenant-a/attest-initiate?target=https%3A%2F%2Fca.example.com%2Fworkloads HTTP/1.1

## A.2. attest-initiate errors

GET /.well-known/est/attest-initiate HTTP/1.1
Host: est.example.com

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request

GET /.well-known/est/attest-initiate?target=https%3A%2F%2Funknown.example HTTP/1.1
Host: est.example.com

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

## A.3. attest-enroll

POST /.well-known/est/attest-enroll HTTP/1.1
Host: est.example.com
Content-Type: application/est-attest-enroll+json

{
  "target": "https://ca.example.com/workloads",
  "freshness_kind": "present-nonce",
  "handle": "VGhpc0lzQVByZXNlbnROb25jZUhhbmRsZQ",
  "csr": "<base64url DER PKCS#10>",
  "evidence": "<base64url Evidence>",
  "binding": { "method": "binding-input", "hash": "sha512" },
  "credential_type": "x509"
}

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/pkcs7-mime; smime-type=certs-only
Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64

<certs-only CMS, as simpleenroll>

## A.4. attest-initiate then attest-retrieve

GET /.well-known/est/attest-initiate?target=https%3A%2F%2Fvault.example.com%2Fsvc&credential_type=x509 HTTP/1.1
Host: est.example.com
Accept: application/est-attest-initiate+json

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/est-attest-initiate+json

{
  "freshness_kind": "present-nonce",
  "handle": "QW5vdGhlclByZXNlbnROb25jZUhhbmRsZQ",
  "expires_in": 600,
  "mode": "retrieve",
  "acceptable_cek": ["HPKE-Base-P256-SHA256-A256GCM"]
}

POST /.well-known/est/attest-retrieve HTTP/1.1
Host: est.example.com
Content-Type: application/est-attest-retrieve+json

{
  "target": "https://vault.example.com/svc",
  "freshness_kind": "present-nonce",
  "handle": "QW5vdGhlclByZXNlbnROb25jZUhhbmRsZQ",
  "evidence": "<base64url Evidence>",
  "cek_pub": "<base64url SubjectPublicKeyInfo>",
  "binding": { "method": "binding-input", "hash": "sha512" }
}

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/est-attest-bundle+json

{
  "group_id": "bGFiLWdyb3VwLWlk",
  "enc": "HPKE-Base-P256-SHA256-A256GCM",
  "target": "https://vault.example.com/svc",
  "handle": "QW5vdGhlclByZXNlbnROb25jZUhhbmRsZQ",
  "encapsulated_key": "<base64url HPKE enc>",
  "ciphertext": "<base64url HPKE ct>"
}
```

Adjust A.4 to whatever `{#bundle}` becomes. If retrieve stays a TODO in `-00`, ship A.1–A.3 only and say retrieve examples wait on the container.

**Normative text:** one sentence in Protocol Overview: “Example exchanges are in {{examples}}.”

**TACRA:** no HTTP appendix. Optional: a one-paragraph command trace (Initiate → Enroll) that uses the same Target string as A.1 so the two drafts can be read together.

Use documentation certificates and a fake Handle; do not paste live SEV-SNP reports unless you have a dedicated sample-data repo (CSR-ATTEST’s pattern).

issues.title: CDDL leftovers: `profile` vs omitted `acceptable_evidence`, and Architecture list markup
issues.author: TheBankster
issues.body:
Grok has flagged the following Important issue and has suggested a solution for it:

Two leftovers in the same pass: a wire-rule hole and a kramdown list that will not render as a list.

**`profile` / `acceptable_evidence`**

CDDL:

```cddl
attestation-initiation-response = {
  initiation-freshness,
  initiation-mode,
  ? acceptable_evidence: [+ text],
}
request-common = (
  ...
  ? profile: text,
  ...
)
```

Prose:

- Initiate: `acceptable_evidence` (OPTIONAL) is “the Evidence formats the EST Server accepts; a request of the second leg names the format of its Evidence in `profile`.”
- Enroll/retrieve: `profile` is OPTIONAL, “the format of `evidence`, **one of `acceptable_evidence`**.”

If `acceptable_evidence` is omitted (allowed), “one of `acceptable_evidence`” is empty. `attest-initiate` itself is optional for `absent-*` kinds, so there is often **no** initiate response at all. A client that omits `profile` (CDDL-legal) cannot be checked against a list that was never sent.

No token is defined for either field (Important #8). CDDL `text` plus “one of” an optional list is not implementable.

**Architecture restrictions list**

```md
Both are subject to the following restrictions:
* MUST NOT generate keys, Evidence, or CSRs
* MUST NOT mint `present-nonce` or `present-epoch` Freshness Handles
...
```

kramdown needs a blank line before `*` or the items are glued to the preceding sentence and do not become a list in the XML/HTML. Same file: `attest-initiate`({{attest-initiate}}) is missing a space.

TACRA does not define Evidence-format identifiers. This is EST wire/CDDL plus markdown. No TACRA change except not inventing a parallel token list.

**Suggested solution**

Define when `profile` is required, what happens when the list is absent, and fix the list markup. Do not add an IANA registry (Important #8).

**EST — field rules** (initiate + both second-leg field lists):

```md
* acceptable_evidence (array of strings, OPTIONAL): Evidence-format tokens
  this EST Server will forward for this Target. If omitted, the Relying Party
  accepts the formats its policy allows for the Target; the second leg MUST
  omit `profile`.

* profile (string, OPTIONAL): the format of `evidence`.
  If the preceding `attest-initiate` carried `acceptable_evidence`, `profile`
  MUST be present and MUST be one of those tokens.
  If `acceptable_evidence` was omitted, or `attest-initiate` was completed
  locally, `profile` MUST be absent.
```

**EST — processing:** 400 if `profile` is present and not in that initiate’s `acceptable_evidence`, or if `profile` is present when the list was omitted / initiate was local. 415 remains for Evidence the RP will not accept (already under Error Handling).

**CDDL** — keep both fields optional; the MUST/MUST NOT is prose (same pattern as `handle` vs kind). Optional comment:

```cddl
? acceptable_evidence: [+ text], ; omit => second leg omits profile
? profile: text,                 ; only if initiate listed acceptable_evidence
```

Do **not** put `profile` in a CDDL group with `acceptable_evidence`; they are different messages.

**Tokens:** none in this version (as in Important #8 `{#alg-tokens}`). If you later add one MTI, e.g. `sev-snp-report`, list it there and in `acceptable_evidence` examples. Until then the arrays are either omitted or deployment-specific strings the two parties already know.

**Architecture markup:**

```md
Neither EST Client nor EST Server has a RATS role.
Both are subject to the following restrictions:

* MUST NOT generate keys, Evidence, or CSRs
* MUST NOT mint `present-nonce` or `present-epoch` Freshness Handles
* MUST NOT appraise Evidence or Attestation Results
* MUST NOT authorize credential issuance or release
```

And: `optional `attest-initiate` ({{attest-initiate}})`.

**TACRA:** no CDDL. Do not add Evidence-format names. The RP’s policy for which Evidence it accepts stays in TACRA as policy, not as EST `profile` tokens.

Check the rendered HTML after `make` so the four MUST NOTs are a bullet list, not a single paragraph.
